title: Canonical character categories and invariant Hopf models
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Use group schemes and their homomorphisms [def-sc-group-scheme], finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum], field extensions [def-pc-field-extension], the recorded multiplicative group $\mathbf G_m$ [def-sc-gm-ga], the diagonalizable group $D_F(M)=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ [def-sfb-diagonalizable-group], and scalar extension and multiplicative type [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. Define $\mathcal{MT}_k$ as the full category of affine finite-type $k$-group schemes of multiplicative type. For a field extension $F/k$, define $\mathcal C_{k,F}$ as the full category of actions of $\operatorname{Aut}_k(F)$ on finitely generated additive abelian groups $M$ such that each stabilizer $\{\sigma:\sigma m=m\}$ is open in the Krull topology. For a $k$-group scheme $G$, write $p_G:G_F\to G$ and $q_G:G_F\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ for the scalar-extension projections and define its geometric characters over $F$ to be $\operatorname{Hom}_{F\text{-grp}}(G_F,(\mathbf G_m)_F)$. For arbitrary $k$-group schemes $G,T$, $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_k(F)$, and $\chi,\psi:G_F\to T_F$, define $\psi={}^{\sigma}\chi$ by the condition $\chi\circ a=b\circ\psi$ in ordinary function composition order, for the uniquely determined scheme maps $a:G_F\to G_F$, $b:T_F\to T_F$ satisfying $p_Ga=p_G$, $q_Ga=(\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)q_G$ and the analogous equations for $T$. For compatible towers $k\subset K\subset K^s$ and $k\subset k^s\subset K^s$, define extension of $\chi:G_{k^s}\to T_{k^s}$ to $\psi:(G_K)_{K^s}\to(T_K)_{K^s}$ by the commuting square with the unique comparison maps preserving the projections to $G,T$ and lying above $\operatorname{Spec}K^s\to\operatorname{Spec}k^s$. These conditions mean the equalities for every pair of scheme maps with the specified projections; such maps exist uniquely by the fibre-product universal property. For any $L/k$, abelian group $M$, and action $\rho:\operatorname{Aut}_k(L)\to\operatorname{End}(M)$, define $s_\sigma:L[M]\to L[M]$ by $s_\sigma(ae_m)=\sigma(a)e_{\rho(\sigma)m}$ and $B=\bigcap_\sigma\operatorname{Eq}(s_\sigma,1)$ as a $k$-subalgebra of $L[M]$. Given a Hopf structure $h$ on this specified algebra, let $D_h(B)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with that group law. An invariant Hopf model consists of such an $h$ and a group-scheme isomorphism $s:(D_h(B))_L\simeq D_L(M)$ such that $s^{-1}$ followed by the scalar projection is the spectrum of the inclusion $B\hookrightarrow L[M]$; this specifies the descended Hopf operations, without asserting existence. Finally, for a character into $(\mathbf G_m)_F$, its coordinate element is the pullback of the Laurent coordinate $t$ first along $(\mathbf G_m)_F\to\mathbf G_m$ and then along the character.
